summary.title: The Founder's Guide to Stock Options (Rewarding Talent handbook)
summary.one_liner: A free Index Ventures handbook explaining how European startups should design employee stock option plans, with benchmarks, case studies and a comparison with US practice.
keywords: how much equity to give employees
takeaways: Stock options grant the right to buy shares at a set strike price, typically vesting over four years with a one-year cliff and then linear monthly-style 25% tranches.
European employees own less equity than US employees (about 10% vs 20% at late stage), and European option rules and taxes vary widely by country.
Option grants at seed stage can be dilutive but may still be worth far more in dollar terms as the company scales, as illustrated by the dilution example.
Stock options help startups hire, retain, motivate and align staff, but only if the scheme is perceived as fair and well understood.
The Criteo case study shows a French company adopting Silicon Valley-style equity for all employees after expanding into the US.
summary.summary: This handbook from Index Ventures, aimed at European founders, covers how to design a stock option plan: who to grant options to, how many, and when. It explains stock option basics (strike price, vesting, cap tables, dilution, common vs preference shares) and compares European and US employee ownership based on research across 73 portfolio cap tables, over 4,000 option grants, interviews and a survey. It includes case studies such as Criteo and references the companion OptionPlan allocation tool for seed and Series A.
